chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the seminal fluid (madhi), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It and the phlegm (nukhama) are equal (in ruling).'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.النُّخَامَةُ: Phlegm or spittle from the throat
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: Seminal fluid discharged during sexual arousal

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for madhi (seminal fluid) compared to phlegm?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Umar ibn Hanzala queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the juristic status of *madhi* (fluid discharged during sexual arousal). The Imam’s response equating it to *nukhama* (phlegm or spittle) establishes it as a minor impurity (*najasa sughra*) rather than major semen (*mani*), thereby exempting it from the requirement of full ritual bath (*ghusl*) and requiring only minor ablution (*wudu*). This distinction is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of prayer after natural bodily discharges.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Umar Bin Hanzala who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the seminal fluid, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It and the phlegm is nothing but equal’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from ‘Umar ibn Hanzalah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Madhiy. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is only like nasal mucus. They are very similar.’”
